title: What The Erhu Knows — EN/ZH/JA (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 100bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal Chinese Japanese philosophy language learning
lyrics:
[Verse 1 — English]
The erhu is a two-string instrument from ancient China
Two strings should be enough for something fine
But between those two strings lives a universe of feeling
That makes every other instrument seem like it's still healing

[Verse 2 — Chinese Mandarin, with English translation]
二胡只有两根弦，却能说尽世间情
[The erhu has only two strings, yet can express all the world's feelings]
弓弦之间，有春风，有秋雨，有泪盈
[Between bow and string, there is spring breeze, autumn rain, and tears]
它不需要更多的弦来表达心灵深处
[It needs no more strings to express the depths of the heart]
两根弦的二胡，装下了整个宇宙
[The two-string erhu contains the entire universe]

[Chorus — English]
What does the erhu know that I don't know?
It's been carrying sorrow since the Tang dynasty's last show
What does the erhu know in the still of night?
It knows the sound of longing fits inside two strings held tight
That's my boy

[Bridge — Japanese, with English translation]
二胡は二本の弦で世界を語る
[The erhu speaks of the world with two strings]
中国の歴史が弓の動きに宿る
[China's history dwells in the movement of the bow]
悲しみも喜びも、この二弦の中にある
[Both sorrow and joy exist within these two strings]
二胡が知っていることを、私はまだ学んでいる
[What the erhu knows, I am still learning]

[Outro — All three languages]
What the erhu knows… 二胡が知ること… 二胡的智慧
Two strings, everything — 两弦，一切 — 二本の弦、すべて
That's my boy
